title: Simultaneous Noetherian local approximation of a morphism of finitely presented modules
statement:
Let $R	o S$ be a local homomorphism of commutative local rings (the inverse image of the maximal ideal of $S$ is the maximal ideal of $R$). Suppose that $S$ is a localization of a finitely presented $R$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra]. Let $M,N$ be finitely presented $S$-modules [def-sc-finitely-presented-module] and $u:M	o N$ an $S$-linear map. Then there is a small nonempty directed set $I$ with diagrams of local homomorphisms $R_i	o S_i$, local transition maps $r_{ji}:R_i	o R_j$, $s_{ji}:S_i	o S_j$, and local cocone maps $R_i	o R$, $S_i	o S$, commuting with all ring squares. There are finitely presented $S_i$-modules $M_i,N_i$, maps $u_i:M_i	o N_i$ linear over $S_i$, additive transitions $m_{ji},n_{ji}$ semilinear over $s_{ji}$, and additive cocone maps $\mu_i:M_i	o M$, $
u_i:N_i	o N$ semilinear over $S_i	o S$. All transitions are identities at equal indices and respect composition; all cocones are compatible. Moreover $n_{ji}u_i=u_jm_{ji}$ and $
u_i u_i=u\mu_i$. The following hold. (1) $R_i$ and $S_i$ are Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]; $R_i$ is essentially of finite type over $\mathbf Z$, and $S_i$ is essentially of finite type over $R_i$ [def-weil-pbc-essentially-finite-type-algebra]. (2) $R=\varinjlim R_i$, $S=\varinjlim S_i$ as rings and $M=\varinjlim M_i$, $N=\varinjlim N_i$ as abelian groups [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. These are algebraic colimits: every element is represented at a stage, and two stage elements have equal images exactly when their images agree at a common later stage. (3) For $i\le j$ the canonical map $S_i\otimes_{R_i}R_j	o S_j$, $s\otimes r\mapsto s_{ji}(s)r$, is a localization at a multiplicative subset, and the canonical maps $M_i\otimes_{S_i}S_j	o M_j$ and $N_i\otimes_{S_i}S_j	o N_j$, $x\otimes s\mapsto s\,m_{ji}(x)$ and $y\otimes s\mapsto s\,n_{ji}(y)$, are isomorphisms. (4) For each $i$, $S_i\otimes_{R_i}R	o S$ is a localization, and $M_i\otimes_{S_i}S	o M$, $x\otimes s\mapsto s\mu_i(x)$, and $N_i\otimes_{S_i}S	o N$, $y\otimes s\mapsto s
u_i(y)$, are isomorphisms. The isomorphisms in (3) and (4) carry $u_i\otimes1$ to $u_j$ and $u$, respectively. Here a localization at $W$ means that all $w\in W$ become units, all target elements are fractions with denominators in $W$, and an element maps to zero only if some $w\in W$ kills it; tensor products are as in [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. All sets and rings may be placed in one common sufficiently large universe.

proof.text: Apply the directed local tower theorem to R→S→S and M. Both targets are essentially of finite presentation over R by hypothesis, and the second map is the local identity. Write the resulting tower R_i→A_i→S_i. Its clauses (1), (3), (4), (5) supply ring colimits, finite cokernel presentations for M_i, and the two adjacent ring localization comparisons and module comparisons. By composition of essentially finite type maps, R_i→S_i is essentially of finite type. Finite-type Noetherianity and localization Noetherianity, starting with the Noetherian ring Z, make R_i, A_i and S_i Noetherian. A finite-type algebra over R_i is finitely presented by the cited Noetherian finite-presentation result, so the chosen finite-type algebra whose localization is S_i can be chosen finitely presented.

For i≤j apply the composite tower localization lemma with (A,B,C)=(R_i,A_i,S_i) and (A′,B′,C′)=(R_j,A_j,S_j). The two hypotheses are precisely clause (4) of the tower theorem. Its conclusion is the required canonical localization S_i⊗_{R_i}R_j→S_j, with s⊗r sent to s_{ji}(s)r. Apply the same lemma with (A′,B′,C′)=(R,S,S) and the cocone maps, using clause (5), to obtain the required limit localization S_i⊗_{R_i}R→S. The identity between the two copies of S is allowed; no equality of A_i and S_i is asserted.

source.place: Tag 00R7, transition and limit localization comparisons, composed by the generic tensor-localization tower lemma

proof.text: Apply algebraic finite-presentation module descent to the directed ring colimit S=colim S_i. Its object clause gives a finitely presented model Q at some stage with Q⊗S≅N. Choose a common later stage with a tower model for M and base-change both models there. Finite presentation is preserved here simply by tensoring their finite cokernel presentations. Conjugate u by their limit identifications and apply the morphism clause to descend this map at a further stage c. Put P=M_c and let Q denote the base-changed model for N at c; write v:P→Q for the descended map. Thus there are fixed identifications P⊗_{S_c}S≅M and Q⊗_{S_c}S≅N under which v⊗1 is u. All rings and modules are placed in one common sufficiently large universe, as permitted by the descent theorem.

source.place: Tag 05N7 (lemma-colimit-category-fp-modules), clauses (1),(2), the affine algebraic case of Limits Tag 01ZR

proof.text: Restrict the ring diagrams to j≥c. This is a nonempty directed tail: for an old index i, an upper bound of i,c belongs to it. Apply final-tail colimit invariance (equivalently its stated cofiltered opposite form) to retain the ring colimits. On this tail define M_j=P⊗_{S_c}S_j, N_j=Q⊗_{S_c}S_j and u_j=v⊗1. Set m_{kj}(x⊗a)=x⊗s_{kj}(a) and n_{kj}(y⊗a)=y⊗s_{kj}(a). Define μ_j(x⊗a)=a μ_c(x), using the old tower cocone on P, and ν_j(y⊗a)=a ν_c(y), using the fixed identification Q⊗S≅N. These formulas are balanced and additive; they give the required semilinearity, identities, compositions and cocone equations directly. On x⊗a the arrow square reads v(x)⊗s_{kj}(a) on both sides, and ν_j u_j=u μ_j follows from the descended limit identity.

source.place: Tag 046Y, simultaneous approximation paragraph; 00QX, clauses (5),(6); tensor universal property, Tag 00CX

proof.text: For either L=P or L=Q the transition comparison is (L⊗S_j)⊗_{S_j}S_k→L⊗S_k, (x⊗a)⊗b↦x⊗s_{kj}(a)b. Its inverse sends x⊗b to (x⊗1)⊗b; balancing verifies the two composites. The same formulas with S instead of S_k give the limit comparisons, followed by the fixed identifications with M,N. They are exactly the canonical maps displayed in the statement, and application to v(x) proves the asserted compatibility with u. Tensoring a finite presentation of L over S_c with S_j supplies a finite presentation of each stage module; this uses only that a tensor product of a cokernel is the cokernel of the tensored map, immediately from the tensor universal property.

source.place: Tags 00CX and 00QX, presentation construction and canonical tensor comparisons

proof.text: The underlying group colimit of L⊗_{S_c}S_j is L⊗_{S_c}S: for compatible additive maps to a group H, define the induced map on x⊗s by choosing a representative s in S_j and applying the j-th map to x⊗s_j. Equality of representatives at a later stage proves independence; a common stage proves additivity and balancing, hence existence and uniqueness by the tensor presentation. For completeness the algebraic element criterion for each directed ring or group colimit follows from its explicit construction: take stage elements modulo the relation that they agree at some common upper stage, and perform each finite ring or group operation at a common stage. This quotient has the colimit universal property; therefore it agrees with the colimits already obtained and gives exactly the representation and eventual-equality clauses in (2). Steps 1–5 now give all other clauses. Empty finite presentations and zero v include zero modules and the zero map.
